title: Love without pretending (Romans 12:9–21)
hook: rejoice with those who rejoice, weep with those who weep; overcome evil with good

segments.voice: Yesterday, a living sacrifice, a whole day offered. Your line was be transformed.

A friend texts: I got the job! And in the chest of the person reading it, just for a second, something can tighten. They wanted that kind of news. They type back: so happy for you!!! with three exclamation points, and they mean it, mostly. Or someone they can't stand has a terrible week, and a small, ugly part of them feels something that isn't quite sympathy. Love is easy to perform. The emojis are right there. Now Paul gets practical: a list of short commands, almost like a text thread. The first one is about pretending.
screen: `I GOT THE JOB!` → `SOMETHING TIGHTENS.` → `LOVE IS EASY TO PERFORM.`

segments.voice: The first line, in the King James Bible: "Let love be without dissimulation." Dissimulation is an old word for pretending. The Greek is anupokritos: without hypocrisy. A hypokrites, in Greek, was an actor, someone speaking from behind a stage mask. Paul's point: let love take off the mask. Then the rapid list. Hate what is evil, hold on to what is good. Outdo one another in showing honor. Be patient in trouble. Keep praying. Share with those in need. Welcome strangers. Then two harder lines: "Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep." Some readers say the weeping is the easier of the two, and that rejoicing with someone whose good news stings is where the mask really comes off. Then Paul turns to enemies. Bless those who persecute you. Don't pay back evil for evil. If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men. As much as depends on you, because sometimes it doesn't. Leave vengeance to God. Then, quoting Proverbs: "Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head." Coals of fire sounds like revenge, but some readers hear it as the burning shame of being treated kindly by someone you've wronged, the kind that might change a heart. Nobody's completely sure where the image comes from. The chapter ends: "Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good." You can hear Jesus's own teaching behind it: love your enemies, bless those who curse you.
screen: `A HYPOCRITE WAS AN ACTOR IN A MASK.` · `REJOICE WITH THEM THAT DO REJOICE.` · `AS MUCH AS LIETH IN YOU.` · `FEED YOUR ENEMY: COALS OF FIRE.` · then, large: `OVERCOME EVIL WITH GOOD.`

segments.voice: Think of someone who has good news right now, a promotion, a baby, a trip, a new love, a win, and if there's a little tightness, notice it honestly; that's all right. Picture their face when they got the news, and let yourself be glad with them, really glad, as if their good news were partly yours. If you pray, you can thank God for their joy, by name.
Anupokritos. Paul's Greek word for love without hypocrisy: no actor's mask, glad with the glad, sad with the sad.
Your line: overcome evil with good. Real love doesn't need a mask. Until tomorrow, friend.

howItsDone: Romans 12:9–21 is sometimes read at weddings and taught as a picture of everyday Christian love; some Christians try to live out "overcome evil with good" by answering wrongs with kindness.

original.note: Greek: without hypocrisy, unmasked. from hypokritēs, a stage actor.

trapdoor: what you thought: love without pretending means always being nice.
what it means: love with the mask off: glad at another's good news, sad at their grief, and answering evil with good.
what a scholar hears: anupokritos, un-acted, and the coals of fire come from Proverbs 25:21–22; one theory links them to an Egyptian ritual of repentance, but the origin is uncertain.
recall: wholeness, the war over, all in its place

chat.says: What did Paul mean by love without pretending?
options: No mask: really glad with the glad, really sad with the sad.
Always look happy and say nice things, whatever you feel.
Love friends sincerely, but treat enemies as they treat you.
chat.meaning: Anupokritos means without hypocrisy; a hypokrites was an actor behind a mask. Rejoice with them that rejoice, and weep with them that weep.
